- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Read on the head. Check-runs at the head: 38 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. Right. No key is refused anywhere, and the run's variable map still holds every key it was handed.
- Public surface: unchanged. Right. The new module is not re-exported from the package entry, and both builders stay internal.
- Half 1 (every container a builder creates has no prototype, the root included): holds at both builders, at every creation site.
- Half 2 (a key with a `__proto__` segment binds nothing): holds at both builders, in any position. Each half is needed beside the other, for the reasons the docblock gives.
- No key reaches a shared prototype through either builder. Tried:
  - the exact name, and a leading, middle and trailing segment;
  - a walk into a value the run holds (plain object, list, class instance);
  - the `constructor` then `prototype` chain, through built containers and through held values;
  - a value that itself carries an own key of that name;
  - the spread and the assign that mount the scope;
  - the map-to-object snapshots and their JSON round trips.
- The descent guard (object-typed slots only) is what keeps the `constructor` chain closed. The pin 'stays inside the run scope, a walk into a held value included' goes red if that guard widens.
- Prototype-free containers and the readers:
  - The CEL evaluator types an object with no `constructor` as a map at every dispatch site read.
  - Member access, `has()`, `in`, indexing, `size`, equality and comprehensions read own keys and answer as before.
  - Results are copied to plain objects before they leave the evaluator, so no container reaches the variable map, run history or the step log.
  - Text holes render objects through JSON.
  - The pre-existing typing fault on a key named `constructor` is unchanged by this diff.
- A security item is with the owner seat.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/service-automation`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: right, on the PR body and the changeset both.

- Nothing an author can write is added, refused or given a new meaning.
- The spec already refuses the exact name as an assignment target, CEL reserves it as an identifier, and the grammar pin already records that no CEL spelling reads a variable of that name.
- `constructor` and `prototype` are untouched.
- The dogfood package publishes nothing.
- If S1 is closed by changing the walk instead of the wording, ② is asked again on that head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Fork, segment list (the order named three, one is skipped): A stands.**
  - Under prototype-free containers and a walk that enters only object-typed slots, `constructor` and `prototype` are ordinary own keys in a built container and are never entered on a held value.
  - B adds no protection to the rule.
  - B narrows two names the spec's key schema leaves legal by ruling, and breaks a printed remedy the grammar pin holds.
- **Skipped or refused: skipped, at the builder.** A builder that throws turns one supplied key into a fault of every evaluation in the run. Refusal belongs at the doors that accept keys, where it is loud and local.
- Escalated to the seat: an author-written key with a skipped segment still parses and registers, and now binds nothing. Refusing it at the authoring door is a narrowing and a contract call, not this PR's.
- Dev flag, reads faulting on a key named `constructor` (pre-existing): not this diff's. It is a reproducible defect and needs its own card. A does not rest on it, and B would cover it only for built containers.
- Dev flag, the held-value write "noted, not filed": not adopted as written. See S1.
- The dev's census of the package's other dotted-path writers: not adopted as written.
- Deviations (worktree, extra real-boot pins on doors that already refuse, the earlier commit title): no objection. The PR title carries no `!`.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, id materialisation or join.
- The PR author is the fleet relay account.

### ④ Design judgment

Nothing declared is taken away at the consumer. For the exact name the skip makes the spec's own refusal real. For a dotted key with such a segment the spec declares nothing readable. The design holds against the code it cites: one rule file, two builders, each half pinned at each builder, and the controls keep ordinary dotted keys, `vars["$error"]`, `has()` and `vars["prototype"]` reading.

S1 (should-fix) — `scope-key-segments.ts` states the rule wider than `celScope` enforces it. Half 1 says a key is only ever an own property of an object the builder made. The CEL walk still writes a dotted key's tail into a value the run already holds when the key's head names it; half 2's own text and the PR's acceptance note both say so. `textTemplateScope` does hold the sentence: it writes into fresh containers only. The rule file, the `celScope` comment, the engine docblock and the changeset all carry the wide form. Either the CEL walk stops writing into values it did not create, or the rule is restated as narrow as the code: no variable key reaches a prototype. Which one is a contract call.

N1 (nit) — `builtin/value-slot-template-grammar.test.ts` (outside the diff) explains leaving `__proto__` out of its list by "the flow CEL scope is a plain object". After this change the reason is the skip rule.

N2 (nit) — the changeset's "no expression that evaluated reads differently" has two edges nobody relies on. A key with a skipped segment no longer creates its leading containers, so a head bound only by such a key is unbound where it was an empty map. A stdlib function that stringifies its argument (`trim`, `joinNonEmpty`, date coercion) faults on a builder-made container where it returned placeholder text.

N3 (nit) — the `it.each` over `SCOPE_KEY_SKIPPED_SEGMENTS` reads its cases off the constant it pins, so an emptied set runs zero cases there. The literal descent pin and the text-hole pin still cover the skip.
